description.narrative: Create a network for learning and sharing of protocols and processes to identify solutions, experiment and generate collective intelligence.

sector.narrative: Structural transformation, including green, inclusive and digital transitions

condition.narrative: UNDP as the Implementing Partner will comply with the policies, procedures and practices of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS.)

description.narrative:
Output 1: UNDP Country Offices and partners will have increased capability for scanning, sensemaking and experimentation for sustainable development solutions in 60 developing countries.
1.1 Number of new data sources used at Country Office level. 1.2 Diversity of different data sources used 1.3 Number of sustainable development solutions identified and documented 1.4 Variety of innovation methods used to test and iterate over the different hypotheses.
Output 2: New sustainable development solutions will be scaled at country level as part of UNDP’s country programme and operations, national policy and/or local markets.
2.1 Learning the Accelerator Lab Network shares with a public audience (outside of UNDP) 2.2 Number of lab insights, processes or products which are taken up by governments or other partners 2.3 Proportion of partners and governments that increase their take up of the innovation methods included in the Accelerator Lab Network suite 2.4 Proportion of UNDP Country Office programming influenced by the Accelerator Lab Network’s work and methodologies
Output 3: A core global level result will be that a global learning and scaling network is established and functioning.
3.1 Size and density of the network effects among the Accelerator Labs 3.2 Number of new models, approaches, and insights documented and disseminated throughout the network. 3.3 Engagement of the broader development ecosystem with published learnings from the Accelerator Lab Network. 3.4 Amount of influence the learnings and methods of the Accelerator Lab Networks have on the discourse of the broader development ecosystem.

2021 – Targets and results (radni dio)
Targets 2021 Output 1: UNDP Country Offices and partners will have increased capability for scanning, sensemaking and experimentation for sustainable development solutions in 60 developing countries.
1.1 5 new sources of data per year
The new sources of data, such as socioeconomic data, financial transaction, citizen data, user journey, ethnographic data, social media, etc. were user through the following digital tools developed in house: 1. TvojCo2 UNDP, through its Accelerator Lab in Bosnia and Herzegovina, has developed an online tool that allows individuals and companies in the country to calculate their carbon footprint in a fun and engaging way, and then offset a part of their annual emissions at the same place, by investing their money or their time in climate action. This place is a web platform www.tvojCO2.ba where the carbon footprint calculator is online and the offsetting marketplace (“CO2mpenziraj”) has been functional. The platform’s marketplace, in its initial phase, offers anyone to digitally buy a tree – and the planting service – from a number of vendors at different locations in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The vendors are mostly forestry companies or public utility companies (javna komunalna preduzeca) which have the legal mandate to sell and plant trees at a public location. Besides the marketplace, the platform offers an event management platform where people can engage in volunteering activities aimed at improving the state of the environment in their communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina. 2. Open Innovation Platform Open Innovation Platform - Accelerator lab developed the Open Innovation Platform envisaged as a digital innovation space that will bring people together and drive collaborative development efforts through open innovations. The Platform promote systemic thinking and innovative perspectives with the power to accelerate sustainable development in Bosnia and Herzegovina and in other countries. It will enable virtual collaboration, creative ideation around different challenges/opportunities, stimulate innovative actions, facilitate learning and future-thinking in society, host experimentation, and showcase global inspirational development practices. The Platform will be up and running by the end of the year, with the first challenge announced on the Platform in December 2021. 3. Open Consultation 2.0 Open consultation 2.0 - Accelerator Lab supported the development of Public Consultation 2.0, a web application aiming to improve transparency, enable public involvement, and collect different views and feedback on different document (policies, laws, project documents, etc.) to be considered in the further decision-making. The objective of public consultation 2.0 is to increase various stakeholder support, reduce risks, and gain broad community support to obtain “social approval to operate” for policies being consulted. The system is to be handover to Directorate for European Integration by the end of the year to enable and support high-quality stakeholders engagement to achieve better public consultation outcomes. 4. Digital Pulse The Accelerator Lab has facilitated the development of the Digital Pulse as a business digital performance self-assessment tool (designed in partnership with the Chamber of Commerce of Luxembourg), which enables a comprehensive analysis of any companys digitalization aptitude in six different areas (communication, management, human resources, ICT and data security, planning, administration and finance, provision of products and services). All these achievements are directly feeding into and informing the next generation programs in the circular economy and digital economy (in development). The Digital Pulse online tool was launched in February 2021, and until the end of June, 414* registered on the platform and made 1286 self-assessments in above mentioned six different areas. The average result of the self-assessments is 33%.
1.2 6 different type of data sources per year 1. Single-Use Plastics Report Accelerator Lab supported the development of Transposition of the Single-use Plastics Directive, and its Impact on the Economy in Bosnia and Herzegovina report. This Report is part of the overall UNDP’s anticipatory policymaking efforts to support Bosnia and Herzegovina in achieving Sustainable Development Goals and creating a low-carbon, circular economy. It offers an overview of the transposition status of the Directive (EU) 2019/904 on the reduction of the impact of certain plastic products on the environment in several EU member states and countries from the region of South-East Europe, as well as in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Report also treats the impact of the Directive’s implementation on domestic economy and showcases the private sector’s readiness to adapt to new legislative and market circumstances through several case studies 2. City of Sarajevo Food Waste Reduction Plan Accelerator Lab supported the development of the Plan of the City of Sarajevo on prevention and reduction of food waste 2021-2025 based on the experience of the Czech Republic. The Plan aims to suggest a solution helping to reduce 500 tons of food waste which are daily landfilled in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Specific focus is dedicated to the City of Sarajevo that is focusing on food waste situation analysis. Based on findings, there is evidence that more than 12% of daily waste disposal at the landfill consists of discarded food in Canton Sarajevo. The city of Sarajevo aims to adopt food waste prevention measures that might have potential to be spread and scaled to other parts of the country. Established Sarajevo Food Lab has been involved in the consultations related to this document. 3. Recommendation for the Inclusion of Green Criteria in the Public Procurement system in Bosnia and Herzegovina Accelerator Lab supported the development of report /case study Recommendation for the Inclusion of Green Criteria in Public Procurement in Bosnia and Herzegovina - Case study of Service for Common Affairs of the Institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The report aims to showcase how green public procurement can be introduced into the practice of contracting authorities in Bosnia and Herzegovina and is the first result of a pilot project implemented by the Service for Common Affairs of the Institutions of Bosnia and Herzegovina with UNDP support. Conference promoting the Green Public Procurement report was organized in November, and rusulted in additional funds for the implementation of some the recommendation. 4. Potential for using mobile and IP-enabled services in public early warning systems: Brcko district case study Accelerator Lab supported the development of a report that analysis the legal framework, practicies and technologies of early warning system in Brcko district of Bosnia and Herzegovina and provides recommendations for introducing cell broadcasting based early warning system. The analysis showcase the current state of surveillance, notification, and alerting in the Brcko District through 4 internationally recognized and applied early warning system components. The analysis also considered good practices from other countries in the region and the European Union to present the best solutions that fit the context and be adapted to legal and other solutions and the number and structure of vulnerable categories in the Brcko District.
1.3 35 new potential solutions per lab per year In December 2020, the Accelerator Lab launched an innovation challenge named “Cisto da se zna or Clean communities inviting innovative proposals from interested neighborhoods or community facilitators on how to make communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina cleaner and reduce waste. All interested applicants were invited to combine transformative actions from at least two of the three areas below: - Area I: reduce waste. - Area II: reuse waste - Area III: recycle waste Out of 35 applications, the best five initiatives were selected for the implementation of their activities in the period January - August 2021 in LGs such as : 1. Banja Luka - a citizen group of the Laus neighborhood in Banja Luka has been contributing to the improvement of the waste management system and changes in the behavior of this local community through the separate collection of electronic waste, composting of bio-waste, and workshops for reuse of discarded materials. Main results: The first electronic waste container instaled in Republika Srpska, 20 composters for households in Laus municipality in Banjaluka instaled and in use; informative workshops on proper waste managemt organized with the usage of specially design teaching methods (coloring book) with kindergartens . 2. Kotor Varos -The local community of Kruševo Brdo has been implementing a project for cleaning wood biowaste from the upper course of the river Vrbanja and the tributary of Kruševica. Cleaning of this waste reduced the accumulation of debris in the lower course of the river, on bathing areas and near bridges, thus created preconditions for the development of tourism and the preservation of natural and cultural values of this area. Concrete results: 70 m3 of waste wood removed from the river Vrbanja; 25 tons of sawdust processed in pellets; alluvial wood processed in outdoor picnic furniture; 3. Gradiska - The Gradiška Development Agency has to offer citizens an innovative mobile application for disposing of PET packaging., Concrete results: Two green islands and two-line waste collection introduced; Bazaar for the exchange of used items and competitions for young people organized; Play green application and competition for plastic waste organized; Gamified learning process related to the proper waste management. 4. Sarajevo - This project was implemented by the Initiative for Forestry and Environment - fea focuses on the Sarajevo neighborhood of Pionirska Dolina, where the plan was to build composting site, and to organize auction of used objects , as well as thematic events and training for the neighborhood. Concrete results:The first joint composter in Bosnia and Herzegovina instaled, info campaign in the comunity regarding composting organized. 5. Zenica - The project aimed to work on awareness raising on proper waste management through promotion and education and eco-actions in five rural communities in Zenica, and the development of an innovative web platform for mapping illegal landfills in the city of Zenica). Concrete results: Web platform www.depotag.ba for community mapping of illegal landfils developed and promoted; Cleaning and education actions organized in five suburban local communities in Zenica. 6. Plasticna operacija (Plastic operation) promo campaign AccLab partnered with “Udruženje za afirmaciju i podršku umjetnosti - Prijatelji umjetnosti” to support an innovative awareness-raising campaign to nudge the public habits towards less use of single-use plastics. The campaign was based on a series of three art photos illustrating the use of single-use plastics in daily life, printed and used on billboards in several locations (Bijeljina, Doboj, Kakanj, Mostar, Prijedor, Sarajevo) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, as part of a country-wide awareness-raising campaign aiming to reduce use of single-use plastic. The photos also depicted unique fashion designs/garments made entirely from single-use plastics, non-professional models, unusual shooting spots (e.g. landfills). The broader billboard campaign told the story of waste issues such as plastic pollution, fast fashion and food waste, in stark contrast of beauty and pollution visuals. The social media campaign was organized through the web-site and social media accounts of the authors of the initiative and through UNDP social media channels. The campaign resulted in vast media outreach and remarkably positive reactions from the people with anecdotal evidence of behavior change towards decreased usage of single-use plastics due to the campaign. 7. A pilot food waste research was conducted along the food supply chain for a single agriproduct to assess the quantities of food loss in Bosnia and Herzegovina, for the first time. 8. SurveyMonkey Accelerator Lab supported the design, distribution, and analysis of multiple surveys as part of research on a) the digital transformation readiness of local governments in Bosnia and Hercegovina, b) women’s engagement in the work of 199 local communities’ centers in the country, c) public kitchens in Bosnia and Herzegovina, d) inclusive decarbonization of MSMEs in the country, e) public procurement regulations and practices perceptions of contracting authorities on the local level and economic operators applying on public tenders, f) analysis of activities of Community centers in Bosnia and Herzegovina, g) MSMEs perception and attitudes towards the transition to circular economy practices. 4. Data mapathon testing WeMapp The Accelerator Lab in Bosnia and Herzegovina supports Ena Kapetanovic, a social entrepreneur, and her start-up in developing a community-based online application that will enable people with mobility difficulties to move safely and independently. This online application named WeMapp will provide personalized routes based on motor ability through a map that contains route obstacles and accessibility detection powered by Artificial Intelligence. Such a tool will offer precious information about the specifics of the outdoor environment and help barrier-free navigation that can be a game-changer in the daily life of persons with motor disabilities. WeMapp app is envisaged as social entrepreneurship at the service of people and urban mobility. Here is the blog capturing Ena’s journey and the idea behind the WeMapp.
Inspired by the similar experience from the AccLab Ukraine, and to support the initial mapping efforts necessary to develop the applications logic further, the testing mapathon was conducted in April with the High School of Civil Engineering and Geodesy students in Sarajevo. The students successfully mapped over 150 obstacles in the center of Sarajevo through the testing application in one hour on the field. Their impression was that there were obstacles on each meter of the public space (streets, roads, public buildings, etc.) and that “everything needed to be rebuilt to be accessible to everyone”. Attached, please find a couple of pictures from testing data mapathon event.
Further development of the app is currently ongoing, and the team is looking for two distinctive outputs of the app:
• developing a navigation app for people with motor disabilities, and • gathering all the mobility impediment data to support the development of policy options and concrete measures to remove those mobility barriers.
The broader Data mapathon, open to everyone interested in supporting this process, will be organized upon completion of the app development.
Furthermore, to help raise awareness about the problem of urban inaccessibility, the Lab supported Ena in kicking off comic book style social media content where she, as a wheelchair user, tells the story of challenges she encounters by trying to do simple everyday things like going to the cinema, or to the city administration to get some papers. Here you can see an example available in the local language.
5. Food security vulnerability assessment UNDP collaborated with FAO in the implementation of a Joint SDG Fund project on food insecurity in Bosnia and Herzegovina in the second half of 2022 and the Accelerator Lab contributed by developing a methodology for the data collection on the population vulnerability assessment and the soup kitchen mapping exercise as part of this effort. Targeted focus groups with selected vulnerable groups were conducted in order to assess the levels of food deprivation among the most vulnerable, while photostories, surveying and storytelling were used to convey the message on the social services in the country that evolve around Zero Hunger efforts. 1.2 six different types of data sources per year 1. City of Sarajevo Food Waste Reduction Plan Accelerator Lab supported the development of the Plan of the City of Sarajevo on prevention and reduction of food waste 2022-2026 based on the experience of the Czech Republic. The Plan aims to suggest a solution helping to reduce 500 tons of food waste which are daily landfilled in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Specific focus is dedicated to the City of Sarajevo that is focusing on food waste situation analysis. Based on findings, there is evidence that more than 12% of daily waste disposal at the landfill consists of discarded food in Canton Sarajevo. The city of Sarajevo adopted food waste prevention measures that might have the potential to be spread and scaled to other parts of the country. Established Sarajevo Food Lab has been involved in the consultations related to this document. The Plan was officially endorsed by the City Council in late 2022. 2. UrbanLab – on-site consultations UNDP Accelerator lab partnered with the municipality of Centar Sarajevo in designing and implementing a new approach for citizen participation in urban planning and reconstruction. The on-site consultations on five micro-locations were a rich source of data on citizen perceptions of the public spaces and provided for a quality design of their future look. UrbanLab – online consultations The same process was then replicated in a “digital twin” of the five micro-locations on the urbanlab.ba platform which allowed for a wider participation of citizens in the consultation and co-creation of these public spaces. 3. Mapping of soup kitchens in the country A combination of methods was used to map all free meal providers in the country and then asses their capacities, needs and user demographic. This was the first effort of this kind ever conducted in the country. 4. Food security vulnerability assessment A combination of focus groups, desk research and CATI surveying was used to assess the level of food deprivation among the most vulnerable social groups in Bosnia and Herzegovina, with a special focus on those who fall between the cracks of the official social security system. 5. Food bank modelling and food security system mapping for Canton Sarajevo Based on the request of the Government of Canton Sarajevo, the Accelerator Lab conducted a food security system mapping and modelled the future food bank to build up on the existing social protection system in terms of the Zero Hunger goal.

Data on visitors to the platform and those who registered and submitted their answers is tracked. The comprehensive report on citizens feedback became a part of the tender dossier for the international architectural competition. The solution proposed reflects citizens preferences. We are soon to publish three winning solutions on the platform and invite citizens to vote and make their choice among those three solutions awarded by the international jury of professionals (architects and landscape designers). 1.4 5 innovation methods per Action Plan. - Innovation Challenge modality including the customized financial and program reporting. the COVID-19 pandemic, informing the specific UNDP CO project • Conducting a survey on COVID-19 impact on women in Bosnia and Herzegovina, informing the specific UNDP CO project • Digital transformation readiness assessment for local governments and cities in Bosnia and Herzegovina 1.2 6 different type of data sources per year • Combining electronic surveying and CATI method to assess MSMEs business expectations in relation to developing pandemic • Using digital solution developed as carbon footprint calculator to track opinions of individuals and business on possible offsetting options • Using catalogues of digital solution mapped by the G20, OSCE and other institutions as options for the country 1.3 35 new potential solutions per lab per year • 15 possible solutions identified as carbon offsetting options for individuals and businesses • 11 solutions identified as digital response solutions for COVID-19 • 104 solutions proposed in the CovIDEJA2020 innovation challenge organized by the Accelerator Lab in partnership with IT industry association of Bosnia and Herzegovina • 34 solutions identified in the Zero Waste Communities innovation challenge organized by the Accelerator Lab • 5 solutions proposed in the Change Makers 2021 UNDP CO internal innovation challenge, organized with purpose to incite more cross-sectoral innovations, 3 initiatives implemented 1.4 5 innovation methods per Action Plan • Soliciting innovative ideas and solutions to address development challenges using innovation challenge modality • Tracking the behaviour of users while using web applications to detect their opinions on different topics • Organizing a series of Future Talks, virtual events organized by the UNDP Accelerator Lab in Bosnia and Herzegovina and centred around pressing issues or inspiring development opportunities. Output 2: New sustainable development solutions will be scaled at country level as part of UNDP’s country programme and operations, national policy and/or local markets.
2.1 6 blogs, or other (substantial) media posts published per year. • TheLabs work was well showcased to a broader audience with significant media presence around the first national online ideathon in the country - covIDEJA2020, the first national CO2 footprint calculator - TvojCO2, the Economic pulse online data dashboard, and COVID-19 economic recovery measures platform, circularity pilots, etc. • A couple of blogs post were published depicting the learnings from the interventions listed above. • Several (social) media mini-campaign were organized to promote the above-listed interventions and digital tools and ensure wider public reach. • Extensive media coverage of the covIDEJA2020 ideathon and its winners. • Several video stories were produced to showcase the interventions results (e.g. video stories about five circular pilot companies and their transformational journey. 2.2 At least 50% of our learning challenges have the public sector as counterpart. The BIH Labs interventions in 2020 had to take a hard shift to COVID-19 response to what was initially planned at the beginning of the year. In these interventions, public sector support was up to 10% as the Lab partnered more with private and civil sector, academia and international organizations. In 2020, the Lab established more than 30 formal and informal partnerships supporting almost all activities and interventions. 2.3 At least one government entity has learned about Accelerator lab methods. • The Lab continued the collaboration with the City of Sarajevo on the topic of Food Waste. • Federal Ministry for Environment and Tourism supported the organization of the first national digital ideathon, covIDEJA 2020. • The Lab also supported the CO project in integrating the innovative approaches in their activities with the different governmental counterparts. 2.4 At least 50% of our learning challenges are providing actionable knowledge to ongoing CO projects. • In 2020 the Lab supported all UNDP BIH sectors in implementing their activities and designing and developing new ways to continue with the project activities in COVID-19 imposed new normal and new interventions, activities, and learnings. This integrative role of the Lab resulted in up to three new projects (Medical waste management, Circular pilots, Digital Pulse) and a vast number of minor interventions related to ongoing CO projects such as Digital Transformations, SDG Bussines Pioneers, Via Dinarica, POPPs, DRR, EU for Bussines/Agri, Dialogue for the Future, Women in Elections, IT Girls, etc. Output 3: A core global level result will be that a global learning and scaling network is established and functioning.
3.1 The lab interacts at least once a week with another lab in the network (48 interaction per year) Result: In 2020, the BiH Lab actively collaborated at least thrice a week with a number of colleagues from the network on COVID-19 related experimentation, shared our insights and practices through MS Teams and WhatsApp groups and conducted a number of bilateral and multilateral meetings within the network aimed at learning and scaling. 3.2 25% of information shared across the network should be methodology, or sustainable development issue and opportunity related. Result: The Lab shared methodology and results on a number of experimentations in 2020 with the network – we presented our collective intelligence work on COVID response and the Economic Pulse experiment during weekly calls with the network, and the results of the circular economy pilots and the CO2 calculator were featured in various channels of the network. 3.3 The Accelerator Lab Network´s work is featured at least 3 times per month in Country Office Social Media channels and tag UNDP Accelerator Labs accounts. The Lab team engages at least once a month across any social media conversation related to the work of the Accelerator Lab Network, from either personal or CO account. Result: The BiH Lab’s work is regularly featured in CO’s social media channels but probably not as often as twice a month, due to the size of our programme and the number of news featuring on our social media channels. All key activities of the Lab are also promoted on members’ social media accounts and we support the announcements made by other Labs as well. 3.4 Connect the Accelerator Lab’s publications to local development ecosystem through social media. Identify and engage with 2 new relevant local social media profiles of the broader Development Ecosystem. Result: Our COVIDEJA innovation challenge and the first FutureTalk were well received in the local development ecosystem and widely featured on different social media profiles. The establishment of the Sarajevo Food Lab was also attractive for local social media.
